title: H(Y|X) = -C: The Key Computation for Row-Symmetric Channels
content:
The core computation generalizing the BSC conditional entropy proof:

For input x with p(x) > 0:
  Term = p(x)·W(x,y)·log(p(x)·W(x,y) / p(x))  [denominator = ∑_{y'} p(x)·W(x,y') = p(x)]
       = p(x)·W(x,y)·log(W(x,y))               [p(x) cancels]

For input x with p(x) = 0:
  Term = 0 (by the if-then-else in conditionalEntropy)

Summing over all (y,x):
  ∑_y ∑_x term = ∑_x p(x) · ∑_y W(x,y)·log(W(x,y))
               = ∑_x p(x) · C                    [by row symmetry]
               = C · ∑_x p(x) = C               [since ∑_x p(x) = 1]

Conditional entropy = -(C) = -C.

Key: This works for ANY input distribution, even degenerate ones, because zero-probability inputs contribute 0 to both sides.
mathContext: This generalizes the BSC computation where the constant C = p·log(p) + (1-p)·log(1-p). For a general row-symmetric channel, C = ∑_y W(x₀,y)·log(W(x₀,y)) for any fixed x₀. The condition C = const is equivalent to: all rows of the channel matrix have equal Shannon entropy H(row x) = -C.

title: Doubly Balanced Condition: Uniform Input → Uniform Output
content:
A channel is doubly balanced if all column sums are equal:
  ∀ y : β, ∑_x W(x,y) = |α|/|β|

With uniform input (p(x) = 1/|α|):
  P(Y=y) = ∑_x p(x)·W(x,y) = (1/|α|) · ∑_x W(x,y) = (1/|α|) · (|α|/|β|) = 1/|β|

So the output is uniform on β, giving H(Y) = log|β|.

For BSC (α = β = Bool): column sums = p + (1-p) = 1 = |Bool|/|Bool|. ✓
For q-ary symmetric channel: each output appears with probability 1/q from each input, so column sums = |α|/q = |α|/|β|. ✓

The doubly balanced condition is STRONGER than row symmetry alone. It ensures the maximum entropy H(Y) = log|β| is actually achieved by the uniform input.
mathContext: A doubly stochastic matrix (where both row sums and column sums equal 1, with |α| = |β|) satisfies the doubly balanced condition with |α|/|β| = 1. The BSC is doubly stochastic. For general |α| ≠ |β|, the condition ∑_x W(x,y) = |α|/|β| is the natural analog.

title: Achievability and Converse: Uniform Input Achieves Capacity
content:
These two theorems together establish the capacity formula:

**Achievability** (`sym_uniform_mi`, lines 143-168): The uniform input distribution achieves MI = log|β| + C. The proof decomposes MI = H(Y) - H(Y|X):
- H(Y|X) = -C by row symmetry (previous section)
- H(Y) = log|β| because the doubly-balanced condition ensures the Y-marginal under uniform input is uniform over β

**Converse** (`sym_mi_le`, lines 170-190): For any input distribution, MI ≤ log|β| + C. Proof: MI = H(Y) - H(Y|X) = H(Y) + C, and H(Y) ≤ log|β| by the maximum-entropy principle for finite distributions.

Together: max MI = log|β| + C, achieved exactly by the uniform input.
mathContext: The capacity $C_{\text{sym}} = \log|\beta| - H(\text{row})$ where $H(\text{row}) = -C = -\sum_y W(x,y) \log W(x,y)$ is the (constant) per-row entropy. The achievability uses: for a doubly balanced channel, the uniform input achieves $H(Y) = \log|\beta|$ since $\sum_x W(x,y)/|\alpha| = 1/|\beta|$ for all $y$, making the output uniform. The converse uses $H(Y) \leq \log|\beta|$ (maximum entropy at uniform distribution).

title: Capacity = log|β| + C = log|β| - H(row): The General Formula
content:
The main theorem:
  C(W) = log|β| - H(row) = log|β| + C
  where C = ∑_y W(x,y)·log(W(x,y)) ≤ 0 (negative entropy)
  and H(row) = -C ≥ 0 (row entropy)

Special cases:
• BSC(p): |β|=2, C = p·log p + (1-p)·log(1-p) → C = log 2 - h(p)
• Binary erasure channel (BEC): |β|=3 (0, 1, ε), rows [1-ε, 0, ε] and [0, 1-ε, ε]
  C = (1-ε)log(1-ε) + ε·log(ε) → capacity = log 2 + C = (1-ε)·log 2
• q-ary symmetric channel: each entry = (1-p)/(q-1) or p, capacity = log(q) - h(p) - p·log(q-1)

The formula captures the fundamental tradeoff: higher row entropy (more uncertainty about Y given X) means lower capacity.
mathContext: The formula C = log|β| - H(row) follows directly from C = H(Y) - H(Y|X) = log|β| - (-C). The row entropy H(row) = -C ≥ 0 is bounded by log|β| (entropy ≤ log of alphabet), so C(W) = log|β| - H(row) ≥ 0. The capacity equals 0 when H(row) = log|β|, i.e., when rows are uniform (maximum noise).

title: BSC Recovered from the General Theorem
content:
The BSC satisfies both hypotheses:

1. Row symmetry (bsc_row_symmetric): For BSC(p) with x : Bool:
   ∑_{y:Bool} W(x,y)·log(W(x,y)) = p·log(p) + (1-p)·log(1-p) (same for all x)
   Proof: cases x; simp; ring — both true and false give the same sum.

2. Doubly balanced (bsc_doubly_balanced): Column sums = |Bool|/|Bool| = 2/2 = 1
   ∑_{x:Bool} W(x,y) = (1-p) + p = 1 for both y = true and y = false.

Then bsc_capacity_from_symmetric applies sym_channel_capacity to recover:
  C(BSC(p)) = log 2 + (p·log p + (1-p)·log(1-p)) = log 2 - h(p)

This provides an ALTERNATIVE proof of the BSC capacity from the more general theorem, complementing the direct proof in ShannonChannelCodingOQ02.
mathContext: The two proofs of BSC capacity (direct via ShannonChannelCodingOQ02, and via general symmetric channel) are both valid. The general theorem gives more conceptual clarity: the capacity formula follows from the structural properties (row symmetry + doubly balanced), not from the specifics of the binary alphabet.
